{% raw %}
`find`: search for files in a directory tree.

## Synopsis

<strong>find</strong> \[<em>path</em>...\] \[<em>expression</em>\]

## Description

<strong>find</strong> walks the directory tree under each <em>path</em> and prints, one a line, every path that matches all the tests in the <em>expression</em>, the starting point included. With no <em>path</em>, it starts at <strong>.</strong>; with no tests, it prints everything.

The paths are the arguments before the first one that starts with <strong>-</strong> or is <strong>!</strong>. Symbolic links are never followed (as GNU <strong>find</strong>'s <strong>-P</strong>): a link is listed as a link, and not walked into.

## Expression

All the tests must hold, as if joined by <strong>-a</strong>.

<strong>-name</strong> <em>pattern</em>
: The last part of the path matches the shell <em>pattern</em> (<strong>\*</strong>, <strong>?</strong>, <strong>\[...\]</strong>, as <strong>sh</strong>(1) globs).

<strong>-iname</strong> <em>pattern</em>
: Like <strong>-name</strong>, ignoring case.

<strong>-path</strong> <em>pattern</em>
: The whole path, as printed, matches the shell <em>pattern</em>; here <strong>\*</strong> matches <strong>/</strong> too.

<strong>-type</strong> <em>c</em>
: The file is of type <em>c</em>: <strong>f</strong> a regular file, <strong>d</strong> a directory, <strong>l</strong> a symbolic link.

<strong>-not</strong>, <strong>!</strong>
: Turns the next test around.

<strong>-maxdepth</strong> <em>n</em>
: Descend at most <em>n</em> levels below the starting points (0: the starting points only). It applies wherever it appears.

<strong>-mindepth</strong> <em>n</em>
: Print nothing less than <em>n</em> levels below the starting points.

<strong>-print</strong>
: Print the path; what <strong>find</strong> does anyway.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 if a path could not be read, or for a bad expression.

## Examples

```text
find /lib -name "*.lua"
find . -type d -maxdepth 2
find /home ! -iname "*.txt"
```

## Notes

There is no <strong>-o</strong>, no parentheses, and no actions besides <strong>-print</strong> (no <strong>-exec</strong> or <strong>-delete</strong>). A starting point cannot begin with <strong>-</strong>.

## See also

<strong>ls</strong>(1), <strong>du</strong>(1), <strong>tree</strong>(1), <strong>grep</strong>(1)
